The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
node_mark_all(child, mark);
```
```c
node_set_marks(node, offset, child, marks);
```
```c
unsigned int sibs = (1 << (order % XA_CHUNK_SHIFT)) - 1;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when splitting an entry that has search marks set, the code incorrectly applies the search mark to all entries in the newly created node (via `node_mark_all`). This is only appropriate for splits to order 0. For larger orders, sibling entries should not have the search marks set, which is violated by the logic in `node_set_marks` that uses the `marks` parameter without considering the sibling count (`sibs`).

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
node_mark_slots(child, sibs, mark);
```
```c
node_set_marks(node, offset, child, xas->xa_sibs, marks);
```
Reason:
The fix involves changing the marking behavior to use `node_mark_slots`, which correctly sets the search marks only on the appropriate entries based on the number of siblings (`sibs`). This ensures that when splitting to a larger order, sibling entries do not receive the search marks, thus maintaining the intended logic of the XArray implementation. The adjustment in the `node_set_marks` function call also ensures that the correct sibling count is passed, preventing incorrect marking.
